title: Water transfer line with two process branches
assumptions: Synthetic study case, not data from an operating plant.
Water is Newtonian and incompressible with constant properties; reservoirs have negligible surface velocity and equal pressure.
K values are assumed totals for clean, fully open fittings at each pipe's own velocity; verify against the actual fittings supplier.
All pipes are full and single phase. Pump curve is illustrative at fixed speed; acceptable flow range is supplied, not inferred.
Gas and liquid relief cases are independent worked checks, not relief loads derived from the water-transfer operating point.
The thermal-expansion exchanger is an independent synthetic relief scenario with its load derived from heat input; it is not connected to the water-transfer pump model.

gas_relief.scenario: Independent critical-gas worked check based on LESER example 7.4.9.1. The supplied ethylene release rate is 4200 kg/h; scenario selection and required load are engineering inputs, not calculated by this tool.
gas_relief.factor_basis: Preliminary effective-area Kd=0.975, Kb=1 and Kc=1 as in the published check. No rupture disk. Gas properties are supplied at relieving conditions.

liquid_relief.scenario: Independent viscous-liquid worked check based on LESER example 7.4.9.5: supplied glycerin flow 5 L/s = 300 L/min. A complete API 521 contingency assessment is outside this example.
liquid_relief.factor_basis: Effective-area Kd=0.65, Kw=1, Kc=1. Supplied Kv=0.789 corresponds to the published G-orifice iteration; this tool does not infer Kv or select an orifice. Vapor pressure 0.01 kPa absolute is a synthetic nonflashing-screen input, not a property prediction.

thermal_relief.scenario: Blocked-in cold side of a liquid-filled exchanger: both liquid isolation valves are shut while the warmer utility continues flowing. Thermal expansion is credible because the trapped liquid has no normal outlet; this calculation evaluates that contingency only, without claiming it governs all other cases.
thermal_relief.factor_basis: Synthetic oil properties at relieving conditions, with the lowest credible liquid temperature and maximum credible U and heat-transfer area for this case. Rigid fully filled volume; no heat-loss or vessel-expansion credit, reaction, inflow or phase change. Saturation temperature is supplied at the same relieving inlet pressure; the utility is cooler than this temperature. Kd=0.65 and Kw=Kc=Kv=1 are explicit preliminary effective-area assumptions, to be verified for the actual valve and low-viscosity liquid.
